newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty slides in light session, O/N fall from highs.
newsitem.headline: Zloty slides in light session, O/N fall from highs.

text.p: The zloty eased against the basket of currencies in very thin trade as banks slowly lenghtened recently shortened currency positions as the Polish money market started to regain liquidity, dealers said.
They said communication problems limited trade to just a handful of banks and that a light zloty-selling sentiment was felt on Thursday, but that the trend may not hold on Friday.
"The market was very thin today -- nearly zero liquidity -- and the zloty lost ground, but the sentiment may change tomorrow," said Tomasz Nowakowski of Bank Handlowy SA.
The zloty closed at 1.79/1.75 percent from the trading band centre, weaker than Wednesday's close at 1.96/1.88 percent.
It was at 2.7855/65 to the dollar, down from yesterday's 2.7825/40 and at 1.8440/50 to the mark, down from 1.8391/98.
Dealers said that foreign investor entry at today's 256 million zloty fixed bond sale was not significant and should not create strong upward pressure on the zloty on Friday.

On the money market, overnight rates fell to 20.5/22.5 percent from Wednesday's 24.4/24.7 percent as the market regained some liquidity after a week-long cash shortage on Thursday's 199 million zloty net inflow and corporate flows.

The market's tightness was sparked by bank overinvesting in central bank drainage operations earlier this month and caused the zloty to rise on the forex market this week as players cut exposure to foreign currencies amid high Polish deposit rates.
On Thursday, tomorrow/next rates fell to 21.5/23.5 percent from Thursday's 24.4/24.7 percent.

At the two- and five-year fixed bond auction minimum prices rose to 93.84 and 80.84 from 93.62 and 80.68 respectively, despite low demand of only 586 million against the Treasury's 800 million zloty offer.
On Wednesday the central bank said Polish net foreign currency reserves, those held by the entire banking system, fell by $35 million in August to $21.925 billion.
Net reserves grew $1.49 billion in the January-August period compared to a $6.11 billion rise in the corresponding period of last year.
It also said broad money supply rose by 1.79 billion zlotys, or 1.5 percent, in September 1-10 to 123.42 billion after a 1.7 percent rise in August.
